# Hypergeometric Functions

![Hypergeometric Functions function icon](../../../../assets/function-icons/functions/math/hypergeometric/00_Repertoire%20Hypergeometric%20functions.svg)

[Mathematics functions](../index.md) · [All functions](../../index.md)

Three fixed operators: Gauss 2F1, Kummer M=1F1 and Tricomi U. Profile hg_ni_documented_abs_real_v1 validates finite inputs then evaluates r=abs(x) only; a, b and c retain their signs. This FROG adaptation follows an unmeasured NI documentary remark. The separate mathematical kernel accepts signed x where defined; these functions are not mathematically even. For example standard M(1,1,-1)=exp(-1), whereas this node at x=-1 returns exp(1). NI scalar baseline: every required input and result is f64. FROG extension through common NumericTreeMath: real numeric Arrays/Clusters preserve rank, dimensions, typed empties and ordered field identities; compatible structured operands combine element by element and each whole scalar operand lifts across that structure. Real f32/integer leaves promote visibly to f64; all result leaves are f64. No implicit Boolean, String, Path, reference, complex, Matrix or NumPy broadcasting overload. Integer promotion may round beyond 2^53. No implicit unwired values.

**Fonctions hypergéométriques**

Trois opérateurs fixes : Gauss 2F1, Kummer M=1F1 et Tricomi U. Le profil hg_ni_documented_abs_real_v1 valide les entrées finies puis évalue r=abs(x) seulement ; a, b et c conservent leur signe. Cette adaptation FROG suit une remarque documentaire NI non mesurée. Le noyau mathématique séparé accepte x signé sur son domaine ; ces fonctions ne sont pas paires. Par exemple le noyau M(1,1,-1)=exp(-1), alors que ce nœud à x=-1 renvoie exp(1). Socle NI scalaire f64 ; toutes les entrées sont requises, sans valeur implicite. Extension FROG par NumericTreeMath commun : tableaux/clusters réels numériques de structures compatibles, rangs, dimensions, vides typés et identités ordonnées des champs conservés ; chaque opérande entièrement scalaire est diffusé sur cette structure. Feuilles f32/entières promues visiblement en f64 ; résultats à feuilles f64. Sans conversion cachée Boolean, String, Path, référence, complexe, Matrix ni broadcasting NumPy. Les entiers au-delà de 2^53 peuvent être arrondis.

## Browse this palette

This entry opens a palette folder; it is not an executable dataflow function.

| Entry | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [Gauss](../../math/hypergeometric/gauss.md) | Evaluates ordinary Gauss hypergeometric 2F1, not a Gaussian density or regularized 2F1/Gamma(c). Reject c=0,-1,-2,... before shortcuts. A terminating numerator polynomial permits r&gt;=1. Otherwise require r&lt;1, or r=1 with c-a-b&gt;0; r&gt;1 is outside the real profile and a divergent unit boundary is singular. |
| [Kummer](../../math/hypergeometric/kummer_m.md) | Evaluates ordinary confluent hypergeometric M=1F1, not M/Gamma(b). Reject b=0,-1,-2,... before shortcuts; negative noninteger a and terminating polynomial a=-n are accepted. Every finite r is in the mathematical domain, although f64 overflow is possible. M(1,2,710) is finite and requires scaling. |
| [Tricomi](../../math/hypergeometric/tricomi_u.md) | Evaluates confluent hypergeometric U, a distinct solution from Kummer M; never 1/M, 1-M or regularized M. For r&gt;0 all finite real a,b are accepted, including integer or nonpositive b. At r=0 use a=-n polynomial first; otherwise b&lt;1 uses Gamma(1-b)/Gamma(1+a-b), including denominator reciprocal-Gamma zeros; other zero cases are singular. |
